subject: Social Media
title: Hong Kong Protests
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Hong Kong Protests.

hook.text: In 2019, Hong Kong protesters used Telegram, AirDrop, and mesh networks. They had no leaders—only apps.

buildup.text: Protesters voted on tactics via online polls. Supply chains ran through Reddit. Maps tracked police in real time.

discovery.text: The decentralized model made it impossible to cut the head off the movement. There was no head to cut.

twist.text: But leaderless movements struggle to negotiate. When Beijing offered talks, nobody could speak for everyone.

climax.text: China passed a security law. Activists fled. The movement that couldn't be led also couldn't be saved.

punchline.text: No leader means no target. It also means no voice.

quiz.question: What key weakness did Hong Kong's leaderless protest model reveal?
